## Pull request checklist

You should familiarize yourself with the files `README.md`, `CONTRIBUTING.md`, and `CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md` in the root of your project, along with the `README.md` of the folder you are adding to.

- If an issue has been created for this, add `(fixes #{ISSUE_NUMBER})` to the end of the commit description. In `{ISSUE_NUMBER}`, please include the relevant issue number.
- Put each asset in the folder that matches its type, and name it the way that folder's `README.md` describes.
- Assets must be free to redistribute. If an asset is not your own work, list its source, author, and license in the folder's `README.md`.
- Sample data must be synthetic. Do not submit personal data, credentials, or content scraped from a live service.
- Keep files small - a sample is meant to be cloned, not archived. Say why in the description if a large file is unavoidable.
- If this PR is not yet complete, keep the PR in draft status. If it's no longer valid, close the PR with an explanation.
